about: Everything a person needs to run the one tree from the first minute: the three workflows, the lists they write to with their definitions, how every workflow becomes a branch through the conditions on its own row, a worked example, and how to pour rows into lists the person already has.

definition.about: Each comment worth answering with a video: the words as written, where it was said, the video made and how it did.

fields.label: Why it is worth a video

definition.label: Comment leads

definition.about: References only, one row per output of the one tree: the id of the row that holds it, the branch that made it, the seed, and the branches that reuse it. The output itself stays in its own list; nothing is copied here.
definition.label: Tree outputs

accounts.why: Its viewers ask the questions my audience asks.

what_happens: A signal-sources row for the channel is written with watching Yes.
tool:watch-my-sources keeps each new video as a signals row (the first read is a quiet baseline).
tool:keep-channels-latest-videos-and-captions keeps captions and the top comments by kind (question, disagreement, newest).
Each comment worth a video becomes a comment-leads row with the words as written.
workflow:make-one-piece-of-content-from-audience-to-publish makes the video with the comment as the audience evidence.
The reply with the video link goes out after the person's yes (Instagram) or waits as reply-ready (other platforms).

pour_into_my_list: The lists here are definitions; pour rows into a list you already keep with tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list. To make one of your workflows fire for a kind of part, write its row with a fires_when list (records:write at @own-records); to change when an installed workflow fires, write a row of yours with only {recipe, fires_when}.
check: The recipes in recipes/workflows.json for these three ids pass recipeProblems with no tool gaps.
waiting_to_publish_why: None: the branches are no longer named here. Every workflow the person has (their own rows, for example an inbox workflow kept only in their account) and every workflow the Workshop installs is a candidate, chosen by the conditions on its own row.
modes_are_selectors: The generic mode workflows (quintillion, infinity, real-life-cases, trillion-x-mode, first-win, follow-through, keep-it-working, make-it-perform, put-it-in-the-world, personalized-reach-out) stay the selectors, each choosing itself by the conditions on its own row; no second registry. Five mode steps gained one pointer sentence each: real-life-cases--case, quintillion--compose, infinity--bottleneck, infinity--continue, personalized-reach-out--follow.
one_use_of_the_tree: The content tree is one use of the tree, branches and leaves structure the person named for their gauntlet and decision method; every workflow is a branch and its outputs are the leaves.
views: Table = the lists; task = the tree's calendar-task rows; canvas = the existing workflow canvas of the recipe. Nothing new is built for them.

workflow:answer-commenters-with-videos: keep-posts-and-comments (with the treg fallback on refusal)
keep-posts-and-comments: tool:read-youtube-comments is the first route for YouTube comments, harvest tool then treg after
workflow:grow-the-one-tree: write-in-the-voice: the outline path (hook, talking points, outro in his own words) beside the full script and the voice-clone path
learn-and-prune: daily retraining of the writing on his edits and results
plant-the-seed: a record wake's changed rows are the seeds when no seed is given
learn-and-prune: learnings as new rows; prune only on three measured failures

choose-branches: every workflow is a candidate; tool:choose-the-workflows-that-fire evaluates each workflow's own fires_when over the typed parts; the AI judges only parts no condition keeps and writes its judgment onto that workflow's row
fan-out: agents_per_step passed on to every workflow run; a blocked branch heals into a condition on an existing workflow or a new workflow row with its condition, in the same pass
learn-and-prune: learnings as conditions and step agents numbers on the workflows' own rows over every workflow; prune only on three measured failures

cut_as_restating_a_mode_step: grow-the-one-tree--show (names existing views; moved to views)
library_rows: a library reference on turning a voice note into an outline
a library reference on offering a free tool to everyone who comments a keyword
pilot: Published with one wake, daily (start_at learn-and-prune), the continuation infinity's continue step names; like every Workshop wake it is off until the person switches it on (wake:switch). A person starts the tree from new rows of any list of theirs with a wake-declaration in their own records naming workflow:grow-the-one-tree, on {record: {resource: own-records, prefix: <that list's row id prefix>}}, input {start_at: plant-the-seed, owner, visibility}; plant-the-seed makes each row the cause names a seed. The decision verdict is recorded (GO, 2026-11-13).
agents: One number per step: a step row's agents is the default (any recipe) and the run's input agents_per_step under that id overrides it for the run (read-data/step-agents.mjs runStep). The trunk passes agents_per_step on to each workflow it starts, and under a workflow's id it sets how many runs of that workflow start, so one map sets the width of the whole tree.
branches: Every workflow is a branch. Each workflow carries its own conditions on its row (fires_when, tools/workflows/branches/fires-when.json): a list of {label, condition: {fields, tree}, made_by, state, evidence}, the condition being what tool:filter-rows-by-rules takes over one typed seed part. choose-branches calls tool:choose-the-workflows-that-fire, which reads every workflow row the person has and every installed recipe (their own row wins; a row of theirs with only {recipe, fires_when} adds conditions to an installed workflow) and lets the formulas engine choose. The 17 published workflows that were rows of the old list tree-branches carry their conditions in the Workshop (recipes/workflows.json); a workflow with none is judged by its words once and the judgment written onto its row. Adding a workflow or installing a kit adds a branch; nothing is listed.
